roles.heroLead: The builder-grade ensuite your Mill Creek home came with is turning thirty, and its tile was never the waterproof part — the membrane behind tile is, when one exists at all. We build that layer properly, hold a 24-hour flood test, photograph it, and only then set the first tile of the bath you actually wanted.
roles.costH2: How much does tile installation cost in Mill Creek, WA?
roles.costP1: Mill Creek tile installation comes in around $14–$26 per square foot installed once tile, setting materials, substrate prep and labor are counted — labor from $11/sq ft on its own. A tub-shower surround runs $3,200–$6,800, and the full ensuite treatment — floor, shower, niche — usually totals $6,500 to $14,000; a bathroom floor alone, about 45 sq ft, runs $900–$1,600.
roles.costP2: The quiet lever in every quote is tile format, not tile price. A $4 mosaic sheet often costs more to set than a $12 slab-look porcelain plank — installers bill for cuts and grout lines, and mosaics are nothing but.
roles.costNote: Mill Creek ranges as of August 2026 · tile, materials and labor together. The number to plan around is the written quote from the free visit.
roles.layersLead: Seven layers sit under and behind the tile you see. Every shower failure we get called to around Mill Creek skipped one — the membrane, nine times out of ten — to save a few hundred dollars on a job that later costs five figures to reopen.
roles.whyP1: Shower leaks bide their time. Water gets by the grout, loads up the substrate, and two years later the ensuite announces itself as a soft hallway floor or a mark on the family-room ceiling. The bill at that point covers framing, subfloor, drywall and re-tiling from zero.
roles.whyP2: About 10% of a shower's cost is the waterproofing. Of everything a bathroom remodel can skip, that's the item that costs the most later.

roles.faqH2: Tile installation FAQ — Mill Creek, WA
roles.faqQ1: How much does tile installation cost in Mill Creek, WA?
roles.faqA1: Count on $14 to $26 per square foot installed in Mill Creek, all-in for tile, setting materials, substrate prep and labor — labor itself starts at $11 per square foot. Tub-shower surrounds price at $3,200 to $6,800, and a full bathroom with floor, shower and niche typically lands between $6,500 and $14,000. The format of the tile drives labor more than its price: mosaic sheets and large-format planks both take clearly more work per square foot than 12×12 field tile.
roles.faqQ2: How much does it cost to tile a shower in Mill Creek?
roles.faqA2: In Mill Creek a standard alcove shower runs $3,200 to $6,800 — demolition, bonded waterproofing system, pre-sloped base, tile, niche and grout included. Add benches, a curbless entry, steam or full-height stone and the number climbs. That waterproofing line is about a tenth of the total, and it's the tenth that prevents the tens-of-thousands repair.
roles.faqQ3: Do you waterproof showers before tiling?
roles.faqA3: Every time, no exceptions. Our showers get a bonded waterproofing system behind the tile rather than plain cement board and thinset: a pre-sloped base, membrane carried up the walls, sealed corners, seams and pipe penetrations, and a documented, photographed 24-hour flood test before tile goes on. Tile and grout only slow water down — the membrane is what stops it.
roles.faqQ4: How long does a bathroom tile job take?
roles.faqA4: Four to six working days for a typical Mill Creek bathroom. Day one is demolition and dust protection; then substrate and waterproofing with a 24-hour flood test; one to two days of setting; and a last day of grout, silicone and trim, followed by 24 hours of grout cure before the first shower. A floor by itself is normally a one- or two-day job.
roles.faqQ5: Porcelain or ceramic tile — which is better?
roles.faqA5: Porcelain wherever there's water or foot traffic — it's denser, takes on less than 0.5% water and resists chipping, so it owns floors and shower floors. Ceramic is the economical pick for walls and backsplashes and does that job well. In Mill Creek ensuites we run porcelain below and let ceramic or glass dress the walls.
roles.faqQ6: Can you install a heated tile floor?
roles.faqA6: Yes — it's the single most requested comfort upgrade in Mill Creek ensuite remodels. Electric radiant mat under tile adds about $11 to $16 per square foot installed with its thermostat, and it only makes financial sense while the floor is already open. Installed over an uncoupling membrane, resistance-checked before and after the tile is set, on its own dedicated circuit.
roles.faqQ7: Do I need to remove the old tile first?
roles.faqA7: Nearly always yes. Old tile removal with haul-away runs about $3.50 per square foot, and it's the one opportunity to check the subfloor for rot and movement and keep the new floor flush at doorways. Setting tile over tile is workable on a flat, sound, well-bonded floor, but it lifts the floor height and hides what demo would have shown us.
roles.faqQ8: How much does a kitchen backsplash cost in Mill Creek?
roles.faqA8: A typical 30 square foot kitchen backsplash in Mill Creek installs at $1,100 to $2,200 — outlet cuts, edge trim and color-matched grout in the price. Mosaic sheets, herringbone, picture-frame details behind the range and slab-look porcelain sit at the top end, because the money is in layout and cutting time rather than the tile.
roles.faqQ9: Can you fix cracked tile or regrout instead of replacing?
roles.faqA9: Quite often. Repair and regrout start at $8 per square foot, which covers stained or crumbling grout, a handful of cracked tiles, or shower corners where grout should give way to silicone. When tile sounds hollow, loosens in a pattern, or a wall has softness behind it, the substrate has already failed and repairs just delay the inevitable — we'll tell you which case is yours before writing a quote.
roles.faqQ10: Which Mill Creek neighborhoods do you tile?
roles.faqA10: All of Mill Creek — Town Center, the original streets around the country club, East Mill Creek — plus Silver Firs, Seattle Hill, Silver Lake, Martha Lake, Mays Pond, North Creek, Thrashers Corner, Murphys Corner, Eastmont and Cathcart, with regular routes through Bothell, Lynnwood, Everett and the rest of south Snohomish County.
roles.faqQ11: What warranty comes with tile installation?
roles.faqA11: You get OC Flooring's 2-year workmanship warranty on tile — longer than our carpet term, because tile faults tend to show in year two rather than week two. Full manufacturer waterproofing assemblies carry the maker's system warranty as well, and since we photograph the membrane and the flood test, the documentation is there for as long as you own the home.
